industry.why: Overweight, carried unchanged and better supported. Component 1 regime, 23-Oct-26 (risk-off confirmed and broadening: the discount-rate squeeze now a positioning wash-out in the artificial intelligence complex with credit leading it, bonds rallied as a hedge for the first time this cycle while the Fed still hikes in December, the US 10-year near 5.10%, Brent $111, French sovereign stress spilling into Italy, European defensives leading cyclicals on all five windows and breadth in the bottom fifth of three years; sources present 2026-W43): two houses now name staples as the place to be, Jefferies' desk (17 Oct) favouring 'pricing-power defensives such as staples and utilities' as energy inflation seeps into core goods and Danske (18 Oct) calling them 'not a bad place to hide'; energy, utilities and staples led the week and European defensives beat cyclicals by 4.7 points over four weeks (37-breadth-and-defensives.md). Relative strength per 31-relative-strength.md, 2026-10-23 against 2026-08-21, not week on week: C now, D prior, so the market has started to pay. Not Double Overweight: the multiples that make staples defensive derate with a 5.10% ten-year, and a defensive destination four weeks into a rotation is a crowded one. The sector rows carry B on Beverages, Tobacco, Household products, Food retail and Food production. Moves to A if defensives lead for a second month with the industry's relative strength at B or better.

sector.why: Overweight, carried, on the special topic 'The UK Budget of 28-Oct-26': non-discretionary demand and proven cases, with the pay floor rising 3.9% in April 2027 against 4.1% in April 2026 and food tariffs cut. Component 1 regime, 30-Oct-26 (risk-off beneath a steady index, led now by credit and the cost of debt rather than by the artificial intelligence wash-out alone: the US ten-year above 5% after a hawkish Fed hold with two dissents for a hike, Goldman Sachs' Risk Appetite Indicator at its lowest since April 2025, euro investment-grade and high-yield yields up 30 and 90 basis points since September, Brent near $115, the French premium a record 150 basis points, Europe rotating to quality, defensives and non-AI growth, the STOXX Europe 600 1.7% from its high with breadth recovering from the bottom fifth of three years and defensives leading cyclicals at four weeks and three months; sources present 2026-W44): staples are the destination of the rotation to defensives, and Nestlé's 4.3% pet care growth read across to ingredients (Jefferies, 23 October). Relative strength per 31-relative-strength.md, 2026-10-30 against 2026-08-28, not week on week: C now, D prior, the market has started to pay. One live holding, Hilton Food (3.30%, Fitness 77.8). Counter-case: input-cost inflation squeezes producers before it reaches retailers. Moves to A with the staples industry if defensives lead for a second month.

geography.why: Neutral, carried as a judgement with the evidence now read both ways, on the special topic 'The UK Budget of 28-Oct-26': the Budget removed a UK-specific fiscal tail risk from the discount rate without lowering it (headroom £15bn, both rules met, the 10-year gilt about 5.32% and its lowest in over a month, gilts outperforming Bunds and Treasuries by about 5 basis points), and the UK data beat on every count (growth 0.7% on three months, employment up 102,000, purchasing managers' indices beating; Pacific, 26 October); against it, 2027 growth cut to 1.0% from 1.6%, unemployment 5.1% in 2027, the energy price cap up about 16% in January, a Bank of England rise to 4.00% almost priced for 5-Nov-26, and banks made the first payer in the next shock. Neutral against Underweight was tested; the data say the consumer slows rather than breaks, so Neutral, with no weight carried in Thematic Fit/Momentum. Component 1 regime, 30-Oct-26 (risk-off beneath a steady index, led now by credit and the cost of debt rather than by the artificial intelligence wash-out alone: the US ten-year above 5% after a hawkish Fed hold with two dissents for a hike, Goldman Sachs' Risk Appetite Indicator at its lowest since April 2025, euro investment-grade and high-yield yields up 30 and 90 basis points since September, Brent near $115, the French premium a record 150 basis points, Europe rotating to quality, defensives and non-AI growth, the STOXX Europe 600 1.7% from its high with breadth recovering from the bottom fifth of three years and defensives leading cyclicals at four weeks and three months; sources present 2026-W44). 22 of the 144 Pool stocks are UK-listed. Counter-case: a 1.0% growth year with a hiking central bank is an Underweight in most books. To D on hawkish guidance on 5-Nov-26, a January price cap above 16% or a spring fiscal event with broad taxes; to B if a second source makes the UK case with the rate path read.
